title: Brandenburg Gate
blurb: Carl Gotthard Langhans’ neoclassical city gate in Berlin, built 1788 to 1791, in simplified schematic form: twelve 15 m Doric columns in two rows form five passageways, and a copper Quadriga of Victoria driving a four-horse chariot crowns the attic.

sourceUrls.label: ad-hoc-news.de: Brandenburger Tor and the Quadriga

systems.name: Doric colonnades
systems.description: Twelve 15 m fluted Doric columns in a front and a rear row, with echinus-and-abacus capitals and no bases, in the Greek manner.

systems.name: Passageway walls and reliefs
systems.description: The six walls between the front and rear column pairs, dividing the five passageways, with reliefs of the Labors of Hercules.

systems.name: Entablature
systems.description: Architrave, metope-and-triglyph frieze with sixteen metopes on each long face, and cornice.

systems.name: Attic storey
systems.description: The plain attic with the Triumph of Peace relief, side steps, and the second cornice and plinth carrying the Quadriga.

systems.name: Quadriga
systems.description: Schadow’s copper four-horse chariot, about 5 m high, driven by Victoria and facing east into the city.

systems.name: Side wings
systems.description: L-shaped flanking wings at lower height in the same Doric order, with open stoas, custom houses, angled roofs, pediments and statues.

systems.name: Steps and platform
systems.description: Front and rear steps and the column platform the gate stands on.

explanations.front column shafts: Six fluted Doric columns, 15 m tall and 1.75 m in diameter at the base, in the front row. The columns carry no bases, in the Greek manner. Exact taper and fluting are schematic.
explanations.front column capitals: Echinus-and-abacus capitals of the front row columns, carrying the architrave. Exact profiles are schematic.
explanations.rear column shafts: Six fluted Doric columns, 15 m tall and 1.75 m in diameter at the base, in the rear row. The columns carry no bases, in the Greek manner. Exact taper and fluting are schematic.
explanations.rear column capitals: Echinus-and-abacus capitals of the rear row columns, carrying the architrave. Exact profiles are schematic.
explanations.transverse passageway walls: Six walls between the front and rear column pairs, dividing the gate into five passageways. Exact wall thicknesses are schematic.
explanations.hercules labor relief band: Classicizing reliefs of the Labors of Hercules decorating the passageway walls. Exact panel arrangement is schematic.
explanations.passageway floors: The floors of the five passageways; the central one, the widest, was historically reserved for the royal family, while ordinary citizens used the outer four. Exact paving is schematic.
explanations.front architrave: The front architrave, the lowest band of the entablature, spanning the front colonnade. Exact height is schematic.
explanations.front metope and triglyph frieze: The front frieze with triglyphs and sixteen metopes carrying relief scenes from Greek mythology, many echoing the Parthenon in showing centaurs fighting men. Exact scenes are schematic.
explanations.front cornice: The front cornice crowning the entablature. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.rear architrave: The rear architrave, the lowest band of the entablature, spanning the rear colonnade. Exact height is schematic.
explanations.rear metope and triglyph frieze: The rear frieze with triglyphs and sixteen metopes carrying relief scenes from Greek mythology. Exact scenes are schematic.
explanations.rear cornice: The rear cornice crowning the entablature. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.attic storey: The plain attic storey above the cornice. Exact height is schematic.
explanations.triumph of peace relief: The large allegorical relief of the Triumph of Peace on the east face of the attic, above Pariser Platz. Exact composition is schematic.
explanations.attic side steps: Wide steps at the sides of the attic, receding in both directions. Exact arrangement is schematic.
explanations.second cornice and plinth: The second cornice above the attic, with its projecting central section carrying the plinth of the Quadriga. Exact projection is schematic.
explanations.victoria: Victoria, the Roman goddess of victory, winged and robed, driving the chariot. The Quadriga is made of copper sheets hammered in moulds and stands about 5 m high. Exact figure is schematic.
explanations.four quadriga horses: The four horses drawing Victoria’s chariot eastward into the city. Only one horse’s head from the original 1793 sculpture survives, kept in the Märkisches Museum. Exact poses are schematic.
explanations.chariot and wheels: The two-wheeled chariot of the Quadriga. Exact wheel design is schematic.
explanations.iron cross standard: The lance with the Iron Cross standard and the crowned Prussian eagle, added when Schinkel redesigned the Quadriga in 1814 as a Prussian triumphal emblem. Exact form is schematic.
explanations.north wing stoa columns: Doric columns of the north wing’s open stoa, at a lower height than the gate’s colonnade. Exact column count and positions are schematic.
explanations.north wing custom house: The north wing’s entablature and custom house, set back from the columns on the longer east-stretching side of the wing. These housed the guards and tax collectors of the Berlin Customs Wall, in force until 1860. Exact footprint is schematic.
explanations.north wing roof and pediment: The simple angled roof and gable pediment of the north wing, with a small circular relief in the tympanum. Exact shapes are schematic.
explanations.south wing stoa columns: Doric columns of the south wing’s open stoa, at a lower height than the gate’s colonnade. Exact column count and positions are schematic.
explanations.south wing custom house: The south wing’s entablature and custom house, set back from the columns on the longer east-stretching side of the wing. Exact footprint is schematic.
explanations.south wing roof and pediment: The simple angled roof and gable pediment of the south wing, with a small circular relief in the tympanum. Exact shapes are schematic.
explanations.minerva statue: The statue of Minerva with her lance in the north wing niche, after Schadow’s 1792 design; the original by Johann Daniel Meltzer was destroyed in the Second World War and replaced in 1951 to 1952 by a copy from the Kranold sculptor collective. Exact figure is schematic.
explanations.mars statue: The statue of Mars, the Roman god of war, in the south wing niche, after Schadow’s 1792 design and executed by Carl Friedrich Wichmann. Exact figure is schematic.
explanations.front and rear steps: The steps rising to the column platform on the east (Pariser Platz) and west sides. Exact step counts are schematic.
explanations.column platform: The column platform the gate’s colonnades stand on. Exact platform depth is schematic.
